plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 3: Polynomial and Rational Functions
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single Cartesian graph showing a rational function together with the two asymptotes it approaches. The horizontal x-axis carries integer ticks from -5 to 5, the vertical y-axis carries even ticks from -12 to 12, and both are tipped with arrowheads. A dashed orange vertical line stands at x = 1 and runs the full height of the frame, labeled x = 1 in orange near its lower end. A dashed teal line of steep positive slope crosses from the lower left to the upper right, labeled Slant asymptote y = 3x + 1 above and right of the origin. The function is a solid dark blue curve in two branches. The left branch enters at the lower left pressed against the teal line, rises to a shallow turning point just below the x-axis near x = 0, then plunges off the bottom of the frame as it nears the orange line. The right branch descends from the top just right of x = 1, turns at a minimum near y = 9, and climbs away to the upper right, again closing on the teal line. Drawing the curve and both dashed lines on one set of axes lets the reader compare each branch against the boundary it hugs. The graph illustrates the case in which the numerator exceeds the denominator in degree by one, so the polynomial quotient supplies a slanted rather than horizontal end behavior.

interactionPlan.concept: When a rational function's numerator degree is exactly one more than its denominator's, long division splits it into a linear part plus a vanishing remainder, so the graph blows up at the vertical asymptote x = 1 while its ends settle onto the slant asymptote y = 3x + 1.
elements: Horizontal x-axis with arrowheads at both ends, integer ticks and labels from -5 to 5, axis label 'x' at right end
Vertical y-axis with arrowheads at both ends, even ticks and labels from -12 to 12, axis label 'y' at top

Solid dark-blue curve, left branch: enters lower-left hugging the teal dashed line, rises to a shallow local maximum near (0.18, -0.9) just below the x-axis, then plunges down off the bottom of the frame as x approaches 1 from the left
Solid dark-blue curve, right branch: descends from the top of the frame just right of x = 1, turns at a local minimum near (1.82, 8.9), then climbs to the upper right, closing on the teal dashed line
Dashed orange vertical line at x = 1 spanning the full frame height (the vertical asymptote)
Orange label 'x = 1' placed to the right of the orange line, low in the frame near y = -9
Dashed teal line of slope 3 through (0, 1), drawn from lower-left to upper-right corner of the frame (the slant asymptote)
Teal two-line label 'Slant asymptote / y = 3x + 1' placed above and right of the origin, near (2.5, 5.5)
Probe point marker on the curve (movable dot) with its x-value readout
Vertical guide segment from the probe point to the slant asymptote, annotated with the gap |f(x) - (3x+1)|
Horizontal guide segment from the probe point to the line x = 1, annotated with the distance |x - 1|
Optional readout box showing f(x) = (3x² - 2x + 1)/(x - 1) = 3x + 1 + 2/(x - 1)

interactions.teaches: Moving a point along the curve makes the two gaps compete: as x nears 1 the remainder term 2/(x-1) explodes and the curve tears away from the slant line, while for large |x| that same term shrinks to nothing and the curve merges with y = 3x + 1.
interactions.label: Probe x-value

interactions.teaches: The dashed lines are not part of the function — hiding and restoring them shows that the curve alone still bends toward two invisible boundaries, and that the asymptotes alone are just guides drawn from the long-division quotient and the zero of the denominator.
interactions.label: What is drawn

demo_steps.title: The curve by itself
demo_steps.narration: Only the solid blue graph of f(x) = (3x² - 2x + 1)/(x - 1) is shown, in two separate branches. Notice that both branches seem to be steered by something invisible: they run off vertically somewhere near x = 1 and straighten into a steep line at both far ends.

demo_steps.title: The two boundary lines
demo_steps.narration: Now only the guides appear: the orange dashed vertical line x = 1, where the denominator is zero, and the teal dashed line y = 3x + 1, the quotient of the long division. Neither line is part of the function — they are the boundaries the function negotiates.

demo_steps.title: Far out: the slant asymptote wins
demo_steps.narration: With everything drawn, drag the probe out to x = 4. The vertical gap between the curve and the teal line is tiny, because the remainder 2/(x - 1) is nearly zero — the end behavior is linear, not horizontal.

demo_steps.title: Close in: the vertical asymptote wins
demo_steps.narration: Slide the probe to x = 1.1. The horizontal distance to x = 1 is small, so 2/(x - 1) is huge and the point rockets up the frame, far from the slant line. Local blow-up is controlled entirely by the vertical asymptote.

demo_steps.title: Cross to the left branch
demo_steps.narration: Move the probe to x = -3. The mirror behavior appears on the other side: the curve again presses against the teal line from below, while approaching x = 1 from the left would send it downward off the frame. Same two boundaries, opposite signs.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Writing f(x) as 3x + 1 + 2/(x - 1) explains the whole picture at once: the linear piece is the slant asymptote the ends ride on, and the fractional piece is the term that blows up at x = 1 and dies off at infinity.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Single Cartesian plot on white, x from -5 to 5 and y from -12 to 12, thin black axes with arrowheads and the labels 'x' and 'y'. The plotted function is f(x) = (3x² - 2x + 1)/(x - 1), drawn as a thick dark navy-blue curve in two branches with a break at x = 1 (never connect across the asymptote; clip at the frame top and bottom). Left branch: comes from the lower-left corner just above the teal dashed line, peaks at about (0.18, -0.9) just under the x-axis, then falls steeply off the bottom as x → 1⁻. Right branch: drops from the top of the frame just right of x = 1, bottoms out near (1.82, 8.9), then rises toward the upper right approaching the teal line from above. Dashed orange (#E8722C) vertical line at x = 1 spanning the full height, labeled 'x = 1' in orange to the right of the line near y = -9. Dashed teal (#1B7B7B) line y = 3x + 1 across the full frame, labeled in teal on two lines, 'Slant asymptote' above 'y = 3x + 1', placed up and right of the origin around (2.3, 5.5). Probe: a filled blue dot on the curve at the slider's x, a thin vertical dashed connector from the dot to the teal line labeled with the gap value, and a thin horizontal dashed connector from the dot to the orange line labeled with |x − 1|. The slider must skip a small neighborhood of x = 1 (snap the probe to the nearer side) so the point never sits on the pole. In 'Curve only' mode hide both dashed lines and their labels; in 'Asymptotes only' hide the blue curve and the probe; 'Combined' shows everything. Keep a small readout of f(x) = 3x + 1 + 2/(x − 1) with the current numeric value of each term.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for an x-value probe: the learner drags x along either branch, a point moves on the rational curve, and guide distances to x = 1 and y = 3x + 1 show why the vertical asymptote controls local blow-up while the slant asymptote controls end behavior.
- Toggle between curve-only, asymptotes-only, and combined views: the dashed vertical and slanted lines appear or disappear over the same axes, making clear that the curve can approach two different kinds of boundary without either dashed line being part of the function.

authoredContext:
To find the equation of the slant asymptote, divide 3 x 2 −2x+1 x−1. The quotient is 3x+1, and the remainder is 2. The slant asymptote is the graph of the line g(x)=3x+1. See the figure.

Slant Asymptote when f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0 where degree of p>degree of qby1.

Graph of f(x)=(3x^2-2x+1)/(x-1) with its vertical asymptote at x=1 and a slant asymptote aty=3x+1.

Case 3: If the degree of the denominator = degree of the numerator, there is a horizontal asymptote at y= a n b n, where a n and b n are the leading coefficients of p(x) and q(x) for f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0.

discrepancies: Source draws arrowheads on all four open ends of the navy curve (top of the right branch, up-right end, bottom-left end, down near x=1); the generated curve simply terminates at the frame edge with no arrowheads.

Default (step-0) view adds annotations absent from the source: a navy probe dot, teal and orange dashed connector segments, and the 'gap = 1.33' / '|x − 1| = 1.50' labels, which clutter the top-right of the plot and slightly collide with the curve and the orange asymptote line.
Left branch local maximum appears shifted right (near x ≈ 0.5–0.7) compared with the source where the peak sits closer to x ≈ 0.2, making the left branch look slightly compressed toward the pole.
The bottom y-axis tick label '−12' is partially clipped at the lower edge of the plot frame; source shows it cleanly outside the curve region.

Axis tick label placement differs slightly: source keeps y tick labels well clear of the y-axis and the curve, whereas here the negative labels sit tight against the axis and near the descending branch.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and mathematically correct reproduction of the rational function with both asymptotes and correct teal/orange/navy color scheme, backed by genuinely useful interactions (probe slider, draw-mode toggle, 6-step walkthrough); main weaknesses are the missing curve-end arrowheads and extra probe annotations cluttering the default view.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; remaining issues are concrete rendering fixes (missing arrowheads, cluttered default annotations, clipped tick label, curve shape detail) that belong to the generator.
